gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Battery Tender 35W solar charger it recommended (SKU 021-1174) is listed by Battery Tender as compatible with LiFePO4 as well as flooded, AGM and gel lead-acid batteries. None states that it ships with both alligator-clip and ring-terminal quick-disconnect cables plus a 6 ft extension, or that its replacement controller fits only the 17W and 35W panels.
standout_why: I compared against energyforthetaking.com (2026-10-27) and solarbatteryscout.com, and checked the sunerpower.com and optimate1.com/tecmate-us.com pages in ChatGPT's results. energyforthetaking lists chemistry and connectors only for the Battery Tender 5W (021-1172), SUNER 20W Pro, OYMSAE, Sunway and Schumacher. solarbatteryscout lists chemistry for SUNER, POWOXI, SUNAPEX and Voltset. SUNER's own pages already state the three selectable modes (12V, 12V AGM, 12V Lithium). The OptiMate pages ChatGPT got already state LFP auto-sensing and recovery from 4V. No result covers the 35W Battery Tender's chemistry list, cables or controller pairing. Rivals already cover the chemistry question for other models, so this only fills that gap for one product ChatGPT showed.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. All three of ChatGPT's product types have a maker-stated LiFePO4 path: the SUNER Ultra through a manually chosen 12V Lithium mode, the Battery Tender 35W per its maker page, and OptiMate Solar DUO through auto-sensing that is limited to 4-cell LFP. So the shopper's 'battery type' answer doesn't rule any of them out. Two things work against the Battery Tender: the maker store shows it out of stock at $179.95, and ChatGPT's card showed $148.30 at Walmart. If the battery has already discharged a long way, the OptiMate is the only candidate whose maker states a recovery floor (4V), but the US 20W kit is out of stock.
